gsm.ctas

gsm.ctas runs the ctas clinical trial anomaly detection engine inside the gsm workflow framework and writes the three files the ctasapp dashboard reads.

Structure

Functions

This package provides gsm-style functions to run ctas on SDTM formatted data view its output within ctasapp or to render an html report.

  • Standardize_Domain(), Standardize_Query standardize data for ctas run
  • Transform_Missing(), Transform_Range(), Transform_OneHot() transform non-standard numeric data types
  • Analyze_CTAS() run ctas
  • BindResults_CTAS(), Summarize_CTAS(), Flag_CTAS(), MakeMetric_CTAS(), Report_CTAS() reporting functions
  • Write_ctasapp() write parquet files for ctasapp from reporting artifacts

Workflow

  • inst/workflow/1_mappings (data specification, filtering)
  • inst/workflow/2_metrics (expect one yaml file per ctas configuration set, as different domains data types may require different ctas parameters, only average for one hot encoded data, custom timeseries for specific assessments)
  • inst/workflow/3_reporting (create artifacts for ctasapp and html report)
  • inst/workflow/4_modules (render html report)

Installation 

install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("IMPALA-Consortium/gsm.ctas")

Usage

gsm.ctas ships three gsm workflow layers in inst/workflow/, so a full run is a sequence of RunWorkflows() calls over SDTM input:

# End-to-end gsm.ctas pipeline shared by the cookbook and the pkgdown example.
# Runs mapping + metrics + reporting workflows against the bundled SDTM
# datasets and stops at `lReporting$Reporting_Summary`.

library(workr)
library(gsm.mapping)
library(gsm.ctas)

lRaw <- list(
  Raw_DM      = gsm.ctas::dm,
  Raw_LB      = gsm.ctas::lb,
  Raw_VS      = gsm.ctas::vs,
  Raw_EG      = gsm.ctas::eg,
  Raw_RS      = gsm.ctas::rs,
  Raw_Queries = gsm.ctas::queries,
  Raw_PD      = gsm.ctas::pd
)

lMappingWorkflows   <- workr::MakeWorkflowList(strPath = system.file("workflow/1_mappings",  package = "gsm.ctas"))
lMetricWorkflows    <- workr::MakeWorkflowList(strPath = system.file("workflow/2_metrics",   package = "gsm.ctas"))
lReportingWorkflows <- workr::MakeWorkflowList(strPath = system.file("workflow/3_reporting", package = "gsm.ctas"))

lMapped <- suppressWarnings(suppressMessages(workr::RunWorkflows(
  lWorkflows = lMappingWorkflows,
  lData = gsm.mapping::Ingest(lRaw, gsm.mapping::CombineSpecs(lMappingWorkflows))
)))

lAnalysis <- suppressWarnings(suppressMessages(workr::RunWorkflows(
  lWorkflows = lMetricWorkflows,
  lData = lMapped
)))

lReporting <- suppressWarnings(suppressMessages(workr::RunWorkflows(
  lWorkflows = lReportingWorkflows,
  lData = c(lMapped, list(
    lAnalyzed = lAnalysis,
    lMetricWorkflows = lMetricWorkflows
  ))
)))

ctasapp

ctasapp needs to be installed and a ctasapp.yml needs to be present and entries need to point to parquet file.

Write_ctasapp(lReporting, strDir = ".", strFormat = "parquet")


# remotes::install_github("IMPALA-Consortium/ctasapp")
# file.copy(system.file("ctasapp.yml", package = "ctasapp"), "ctasapp.yml")
# embedded:
#   results: results.parquet
#   input: input.parquet
#   untransformed: untransformed.parquet
#   queries: queries.parquet
#   pd: pd.parquet

ctasapp::run_ctas_app()

html Report 


lModuleFlows <- workr::MakeWorkflowList(strPath = system.file("workflow/4_modules", package = "gsm.ctas"))

workr::RunWorkflows(
  lWorkflows = lModuleFlows,
  lData = lReporting
)

Extending

new data fields can be added via the 1_mappings workflows and need to be taken up in 2_metrics for processing by either one of the exisiting configurations or by creating a new one. One config file per ctas run parameter configuration.

Example

Score sites on a single numeric SDTM field (systolic blood pressure) using only gsm.ctas functions, straight from raw SDTM to CTAS results:

library(gsm.ctas)

dfSubjects <- data.frame(
  studyid    = gsm.ctas::dm$STUDYID,
  subject_id = gsm.ctas::dm$USUBJID,
  site       = gsm.ctas::dm$SITEID,
  country    = gsm.ctas::dm$COUNTRY
)

dfInput <- Standardize_Domain(
  dfDomain     = subset(gsm.ctas::vs, VSTESTCD == "SYSBP"),
  dfSubjects   = dfSubjects,
  strTestCDCol = "VSTESTCD",
  strTestCol   = "VSTEST",
  strValueCol  = "VSSTRESN",
  strCategory  = "Vital Signs"
)

head(dfInput)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 17
#>   subject_id  parameter_id parameter_name          parameter_category_1
#>   <chr>       <chr>        <chr>                   <chr>               
#> 1 01-701-1015 SYSBP        Systolic Blood Pressure Vital Signs         
#> 2 01-701-1015 SYSBP        Systolic Blood Pressure Vital Signs         
#> 3 01-701-1015 SYSBP        Systolic Blood Pressure Vital Signs         
#> 4 01-701-1015 SYSBP        Systolic Blood Pressure Vital Signs         
#> 5 01-701-1015 SYSBP        Systolic Blood Pressure Vital Signs         
#> 6 01-701-1015 SYSBP        Systolic Blood Pressure Vital Signs

#> #   visit <chr>, visitnum <int>, timepoint_1_name <chr>,
#> #   timepoint_2_name <chr>, timepoint_rank <int>, value <dbl>, result <dbl>,
#> #   baseline <dbl>, studyid <chr>, site <chr>, country <chr>

dfResults <- Analyze_CTAS(
  dfInput                 = dfInput,
  bAutocorr               = TRUE,
  bAverage                = TRUE,
  bSD                     = TRUE,
  bRange                  = FALSE,
  bUniqueValueCountRelative = TRUE,
  bOwnSiteSimilScore      = FALSE,
  bLOF                    = FALSE,
  nMinTimepoints          = 1,
  nMinSubjects            = 3,
  dMaxShareMissing        = 0.5,
  bChangeFromBaseline     = FALSE,
  bAutogenerate           = TRUE,
  strScoringMethod        = "ks",
  strPadjustMethod        = "fdr",
  dfCustomTimeseries      = ctas::ctas_data$custom_timeseries,
  dfCustomReferenceGroups = ctas::ctas_data$custom_reference_groups,
  nSeed                   = 1,
  strStudyCol             = "studyid"
)

Contributing

Issues and pull requests are welcome. Please use the issue templates in .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/ and see the Contributor Guidelines vignette for branch conventions, the development process, and the full list of required CI checks.

Exported functions follow a stage-based naming scheme – Input_* (SDTM to CTAS input), Prepare_* (make values comparable), Analyze_* (run CTAS and emit ctasapp shards), Combine_* and Write_* (assemble and export). Note that Transform_* is not used, as it carries a specific and different meaning within gsm itself.

Quality Control

gsm.ctas adopts the IMPALA-Consortium quality-control model documented on the sister package gsm.simaerep:

  • 100% line coverage. Coverage is enforced in CI by test-coverage-strict.yaml, which hard-fails when covr::percent_coverage() is below 100. The existing test-coverage.yaml continues to publish the coverage badge via the shared gsm.utils/test-coverage-core.yaml reporter.
  • No # nocov markers. Every line of R/ runs under the test suite, including the HTML rendering pipeline. Widget builders in R/utils_Charts.R are exercised directly in tests/testthat/test-utils_Charts.R with expect_s3_class(..., "htmlwidget") – mirroring gsm.simaerep/tests/testthat/test_widgets.R – and the end-to-end Report_CTAS() render is exercised through the report_ctas_site module in tests/testthat/test_workflow.R with withr::local_tempdir() – mirroring gsm.simaerep/tests/testthat/test_workflow.R.
  • Unit tests. Every core function has a direct unit test. File I/O (including Write_ctasapp()), input validation, data preparation and every other non-render code path is covered by a targeted testthat file.
  • Arrow is always tested. arrow is a Suggests dependency and is installed on every CI runner, so the parquet round-trip in Write_ctasapp() is exercised on every push.
  • Package checks. R CMD check runs across the OS/R-version matrix in R-CMD-check.yaml and must be clean before a pull request can merge.
  • Documentation. Every exported function carries roxygen docs with runnable @examples; devtools::document() must produce no unstaged diff. Maintainers can post /document on a pull request to run this in CI via pr-commands.yaml.
  • Code formatting. Code is formatted with styler::style_pkg(). Maintainers can post /style on a pull request to run this in CI.
  • Contributor guidelines. Branch and development-process rules live in vignette("ContributorGuidelines").
  • Cookbook. Usage patterns are demonstrated in vignette("gsm-ctas").
